title: A recall prompt that isn't assessment
statement: Keep a commit-before-reveal prompt, such as saying a word's meaning before turning its card, as retrieval practice, but never count it as assessment, since nothing checks the answer.
detail: When a review of a Grade 9 prototype cut a deck of word cards, it kept the deck's prompt to say what each word means before turning it over, and moved it into the word web. Its evidence note says attempting to retrieve before seeing the answer produces better retention than studying the answer alone, but that the prompt is unverifiable and so should not be counted as assessment; the note names no study. A lesson build for the play's next act asks learners to say a definition aloud before unsealing each term.
